title: Philly Cheesesteak Sliders
shortDescription: Chopped steak sliders with peppers and provolone for ten
subtitle: Chopped steak sliders with peppers and provolone for ten
description: Thin-sliced ribeye is chopped with peppers and onions on a griddle, piled onto slider buns with provolone, and baked until melted. A quick au jus on the side keeps everything juicy.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Philly Cheesesteak Sliders in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Sauté peppers and onions
steps.instruction: Heat oil on a griddle or large skillet over medium-high. Cook peppers and onions with salt until softened and lightly charred, about 8 minutes. Push to the side.

steps.title: Chop and cook steak
steps.instruction: Add sliced ribeye in a single layer, season with salt and pepper, and sear 2 minutes. Chop with spatulas and cook until no pink remains and edges crisp, about 5–6 minutes total.

steps.title: Combine and melt cheese
steps.instruction: Mix steak with peppers and onions. Lay provolone over the mixture and cover until cheese melts completely, about 2 minutes. Keep warm while you prep buns.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.instruction: Split slider buns in connected sheets on a foil-lined pan. Pile steak mixture on bottoms, cap with tops, and bake at 350°F for 10 minutes until buns toast lightly. Target oven/smoker temperature: 350°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Philly Cheesesteak Sliders onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Make au jus and serve
steps.instruction: Simmer beef broth with Worcestershire 5 minutes. Slice sliders along seams, serve with small cups of au jus for dunking while cheese is still melted.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Philly Cheesesteak Sliders — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Partially frozen ribeye slices thin like deli meat—warm steak shreds instead of slicing.
American cheese melts smoother than provolone if you want maximum goo factor.
Do not overfill—sliders need room to close without blowing out during baking.
tonightSpread: Cheesesteak sliders with au jus cups and a tray of oven fries.
Shaker of dried oregano and hot cherry peppers for Philly purists at the table.
leftovers: Reheat in foil at 325°F with a splash of broth to restore juiciness.
Chop filling into a breakfast omelet with hot sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cheesesteaks are messy in a good way—these sliders keep the flavor but reduce drip risk on the couch. They portion cleanly and reheat in foil packs for second-half hunger.
mealPrepNotes: Slice ribeye paper-thin when partially frozen for easier cutting. Peppers and onions can be sautéed ahead and reheated on the griddle. Freeze steak 20 minutes before slicing.
